Topics · The holy books together

Did Jesus really say "this is a straight path"?

Three times the Quran reports Jesus calling worship of his Lord a straight path. See what the Gospels hold.

Part 1 of 3

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۗ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is the straight path.'"

Quran · Aal Imran 3:51

Translation

Jesus said to him, “‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’ This is the first and great commandment. A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ The whole law and the prophets depend on these two commandments.”

Original · Ancient Greek

ὁ δὲ ἔφη αὐτῷ· Ἀγαπήσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ καρδίᾳ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ ψυχῇ σου καὶ ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ διανοίᾳ σου· αὕτη ἐστὶν ἡ μεγάλη καὶ πρώτη ἐντολή. Δευτέρα δὲ ὁμοία αὐτῇ· Ἀγαπήσεις τὸν πλησίον σου ὡς σεαυτόν. ἐν ταύταις ταῖς δυσὶν ἐντολαῖς ὅλος ὁ νόμος κρέμαται καὶ οἱ προφῆται.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 22:37-40

World English Bible

﴿وَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[Jesus said], "And indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. That is a straight path."

Quran · Maryam 19:36

﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."

Quran · Az-Zukhruf 43:64

Let us be plain first. This sentence comes from the Quran, which reports it three times, in three chapters, always in one shape: God is my Lord and yours, worship Him, this is a straight path. So ask what kind of claim this is. It is a report of what Jesus taught, from a book that came centuries later. A reader can weigh such a report against what else is known of his teaching.

A question for you

How does this sentence strike you?

If you sayIt is not in the Gospels, so he did not say it
ThenA fair place to begin, and this Step grants it. The Quran does not ask you to find the sentence there. It asks whether the content fits what you do find. That comes next.
If you sayIt sounds like him
ThenThen you hear a family likeness. Likeness is not yet proof, so let us see how far it runs.
If you sayHe said something greater: I am the way
ThenThose are the words most Christians hold to, and they deserve a whole Step of their own, which is open to you.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَمَّا جَآءَ عِيسَىٰ بِٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ قَالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكُم بِٱلْحِكْمَةِ وَلِأُبَيِّنَ لَكُم بَعْضَ ٱلَّذِى تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ ۖ فَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُونِ٦٣ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ رَبِّى وَرَبُّكُمْ فَٱعْبُدُوهُ ۚ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ٦٤﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when Jesus brought clear proofs, he said, "I have come to you with wisdom [i.e., prophethood] and to make clear to you some of that over which you differ, so fear Allāh and obey me. Indeed, Allāh is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path."

Quran · Az-Zukhruf 43:63-64

Now to the Gospels. They open with a voice in the wilderness calling people to prepare the Lord's way and make His paths straight. Jesus speaks of a narrow gate and a road that leads to life. When everything is offered him for one act of worship, he replies that worship is for God alone. His first followers were known as people of the Way. So worship of God alone and a road to walk are both in the texts you hold. The verse joins them in one sentence.

A question for you

In the Gospels as you know them, what is the way he called people to?

If you sayLoving God and neighbour
ThenThen you have named the two commandments he called the greatest, and they start from the one God. The verse calls that worship.
If you sayFollowing him
ThenThen the question is where following him leads. Whoever follows him does what he did. The verse gives the direction: my Lord and yours.
If you sayFaith in his death and resurrection
ThenThat is the centre of the Church's preaching, and it has its own Step. For now, notice that the path in the verse is made of worship.

Part 3 of 3

﴿قُلْ إِنَّنِى هَدَىٰنِى رَبِّىٓ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ دِينًا قِيَمًا مِّلَّةَ إِبْرَٰهِيمَ حَنِيفًا ۚ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path - a correct religion - the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not among those who associated others with Allāh."

Quran · Al-An'am 6:161

Translation

Moreover, as for me, far be it from me that I should sin against Yahweh in ceasing to pray for you; but I will instruct you in the good and the right way.

Original · Hebrew

גַּ֣ם אָנֹכִ֗י חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵחֲטֹ֣א לַֽיהוָ֔ה מֵחֲדֹ֖ל לְהִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעַדְכֶ֑ם וְהוֹרֵיתִ֣י אֶתְכֶ֔ם בְּדֶ֥רֶךְ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה וְהַיְשָׁרָֽה׃

1 Samuel · 12:23

World English Bible

﴿وَأَنِ ٱعْبُدُونِى ۚ هَـٰذَا صِرَٰطٌ مُّسْتَقِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And that you worship [only] Me? This is a straight path.

Quran · Ya-Sin 36:61

The same words are given to others. The Quran's Prophet is told to say his Lord guided him to a straight path, the way of Abraham. God tells all the children of Adam that to worship Him is a straight path. So if Jesus said it, he said nothing that was his alone. That is the Quran's one path: many messengers, one direction. It is also what it means by Islam: the surrender they all taught, with its final law in what Muhammad brought. That claim is yours to weigh.

A question for you

If the road is one, what would you expect those walking it to have in common?

If you sayWorship of the one God
ThenThat is what the verses name. It follows that someone on it may not carry your name, and that a name alone puts no one on it.
If you sayLove and doing good
ThenThe verses treat worship and deed as one thing: worship that shows in conduct. The question is what love is when it has no one it is finally turned toward.
If you sayBelonging to Christ
ThenThat is the answer of one who believes the way is Christ himself. In the verse the path is something pointed to, and Jesus is the one pointing. Weigh the two together.

Your reflection

If you had to describe the road you are walking to a stranger in one sentence, with no religious words, what would you say?
